The World’s Most Powerful Women 2024
EDITED BY
MOIRA FORBES
,
MAGGIE MCGRATH
,
ERIN SPENCER SAIRAM
AND
ERIKA BURHO
DECEMBER 11, 2024, 06:30 AM
After Claudia Sheinbaum took the oath of office as Mexico’s president in October, a historic cheer filled the congressional chamber:
“Presidenta! Presidenta!”
Sheinbaum, 62, is the first woman to preside over the nation—the world’s 12th-largest economy—in its 200 year history as an independent country. “Many of us were told a version of history since we were children, which wanted us to believe that the course of humanity was led only by men. But little by little this vision has been reversed,” she said in her inauguration speech. “It is time for women.”
The women on the 2024 Power Women list define this moment. It is determined by four main metrics: money, media, impact and spheres of influence. The result: 100 women across finance, technology, media and beyond who command a collective $33 trillion in economic power and influence more than 1 billion people.
CLICK HERE FOR THE FULL STORY AND METHODOLOGY.
The Highlights
Malina Ngai
Malina Ngai became Group CEO of AS Watson, an international health and beauty retailer with $23 billion in revenue and 16,800 stores worldwide, in May. She joined the company in 2001 and was most recently its Group Chief Operating Officer and head of Europe and Asia businesses. In her first address to the company as CEO, Ngai called herself a “team captain,” a phrase rooted in the earliest part of her career: A one-time elite rower, Ngai won a bronze medal in the 1994 Asian Games.
View Profile
Janet Truncale
In July, Janet Truncale officially took office as EY’s Global Chair and CEO—and, in so doing, became the first woman to lead a Big Four audit firm. As head of a company with more than $50 billion in annual revenue and some 400,000 employees across the globe, Truncale has come a long way from her earliest days at EY: she started as an intern in 1991. Before her promotion to EY’s CEO, Truncale served as EY Vice Chair and Regional Managing Partner of the Americas Financial Services Organization.
View Profile
Nirmala Sitharaman
Economist Nirmala Sitharaman became India's minister of finance and minister of corporate affairs in May 2019; she is the first full-time female minister to hold both positions. As finance chief, Sitharaman oversees a nearly $4 trillion economy, the fifth largest in the world. She projects that India’s GDP will soon overtake both Japan and Germany, becoming the third-largest in the world by 2027. Sitharaman has been outspoken in favor of women’s economic empowerment in India, encouraging entrepreneurship, business lending and financial education for her country’s female population.
View Profile
Bela Bajaria
One of the most powerful women in television, Bela Bajaria was named Netflix's chief content officer in January 2023. As head of one of the world’s largest streamers (it has 283 million paid memberships across 190 countries), Bajaria is in charge of a $17 billion annual content budget and is responsible for hits including “Bridgerton” and “Lupin.” Before joining Netflix in 2016, Bajaria was president of Universal Television, where she made history as the first woman of color to oversee a studio. In October, she also joined the Coca-Cola board of directors.
